rat_arc_hfd_gse232510.basis: Registered arcuate track, sedentary HFD minus sedentary chow in female rat ARC. The registered R 4.6.0 edgeR-QL groupcase coefficient uses GSM7349354–GSM7349356 as controls and GSM7349357–GSM7349359 as cases. The study reports Wistar rats.

Figure 4C gives sample labels and a caption count of 80 genes, with no gene row labels. No full list for the reported 966 increases and 748 decreases was located.

Use the authors’ case-minus-control orientation and all six additional explicit transcriptomic directions. The v2 selected-reference denominator is 14. The authors give no fit-level library list or animal-to-library mapping.

Report deposited and registered CRD-minus-control values, nominal raw P < 0.05 and BH FDR < 0.05. Leave missing author statistics unassessed and apply the author-concordance-v2 minimum of 30 paired genes.

Report shared rows separately and distinguish Cirbp’s inferred membership from explicit region labels.

The full author testing universe remains unverified.

The 19 yellow and four cyan hypothalamus cells agree with the registered signs. The heatmap bins do not identify exact effect sizes for correlation or magnitude comparisons.

Figure 6B shows hypothalamic discoveries in both directions. The registered fit has zero. The five explicit hypothalamus labels preceding the repeated rows are Fam13b, Fkbp9, Gpt2, Mapk4 and Trim2. Cross-region signature selection excludes posterior hippocampus and counts 14 eligible brain regions. Full author testing coverage and the identities of all hypothalamic discoveries remain unknown.

mouse_hypo_dr_gse227689.criteria: Use every printed row in the labeled hypothalamus column, exact gene symbols, the cyan-to-yellow log2FC scale and the published aDR-minus-AL orientation. All 23 directional pairs were usable, below the author-concordance-v2 minimum of 30. Exact numeric author effects needed for Pearson, Spearman and magnitude comparisons are unavailable.

The conflicting treatment and region labels limit gene-level interpretation. Full verification and author-concordance-v2 acceptance remain unsupported.

Reverse the sign of each plotted x coordinate for diestrus minus estrus.

For the four figure readings, Pearson is 0.480, Spearman is 0.400 and the median and maximum absolute differences are about 1.67 and 3.78 log2 units.

Figure 1C shows aggregate DEG counts. Neither source supplies gene-wise expression P or q for the four pairs. The registered limma fit used a BH family of 18,838 tested rows, including 103 unmapped rows. Zero of the 18,735 published genes have BH FDR < 0.05.

coverage.note: Eight hypothalamus regulators appear in both relevant sheets of Table 1. Five marker cores pass the size and color rule. Four distinct gene assignments survive both-axis matching. One core is ambiguous between Ehf and Elf3, and two factors have no locatable core. Four pairs cover 50% of the eight selected factors and 0.02135% of the 18,735 published registered genes.

mouse_hypo_estrous_cycle_gse131172.criteria: Use all eight author-selected hypothalamus regulators and every identifiable plotted expression estimate. Under author-concordance-v2, ≥30 pairs and ≥90% relevant coverage are required along with compatible cohort, contrast, identifiers and effect definitions. Both correlations must reach 0.90, or ≥90% direction agreement must hold across ≥30 nonzero pairs covering ≥90% of all pairs. Report magnitudes and inference as context.

Both correlations are below 0.90. This comparison supports a detailed review of selected effects, with no full contrast sign-off.

Four cells labeled March 1 or March 2 have competing Marc and March symbols. Their worksheet row IDs keep them unpaired. Marc2, March1 and March2 are the three unpaired registered symbols. No effect, P value or FDR entered these assignments.

All 16,906 paired effects are nonzero and 16,575 agree in sign (98.0421%). The median absolute difference is 0.00349127 log2 units and the registered-to-author RMS effect ratio is 0.98069750. A further 3,513 intact source symbols lie outside the registered table and four source identifiers remain ambiguous. Every paired gene has both raw P and adjusted P in both tables.

All seven paired effects are positive. Pearson r = 0.953409 and Spearman rho = 0.928571. The median absolute log2 difference is 0.194034 and the maximum is 1.292263 for Hspa1a.

At FDR < 0.05 the counts are seven author, six local and six shared within S2. Sixty-six of 72 local FDR calls and two of five local paper-rule calls have no S2 row. Author raw P and all missing author statistics remain unassessed.

coverage.note: All seven author-selected HSP genes pair with the registered table of 33,714 published genes. The local BH correction covered 35,402 fitted rows. The paper’s 68 known hypothalamic DEGs exclude novel genes. Tables S3 and S4 identify 47 distinct Ensembl IDs among the enriched terms. Their P values apply to the terms. The reviewed sources lack the complete gene-level author result.

mouse_hypo_heat_stress_gse128660.criteria: Use all seven rows of the source-defined hypothalamus section, their original signs and exact symbol matches. Apply BH-adjusted P < 0.01 and absolute log2 fold change > log2(1.5), using the Methods and Results and the reported upregulated and downregulated discoveries. The Figure 3D legend uses an inclusive 1.5-fold boundary. No hypothalamic S2 or registered effect is on that boundary, so either convention gives the same calls here. Also report FDR < 0.05 on finite pairs. Author-concordance-v2 requires at least 30 effect pairs, at least 90% relevant coverage and compatible cohort, contrast, identifiers and effect definitions. The correlation route requires both Pearson and Spearman ≥ 0.90. The direction route requires ≥ 90% agreement among at least 30 nonzero pairs covering ≥ 90% of all pairs.

The paper does not identify the P column used for the figure. Of the 80 panel genes, 66 have registered raw P < 0.05 and 33 have registered FDR < 0.05. The response describes Crh as significantly increased. Its registered log2FC is +0.31638, raw P is 0.21230 and FDR is 0.49633. Exact author P values and FDRs are unavailable for paired comparisons.

coverage.note: All 80 labeled rows pair. Both manuscript versions link Figure 5A to 80 genes with a HIF1β promoter motif and report 313 upregulated hypothalamic genes. The peer-review response describes the panel as all genes passing the LFC and P cutoffs. The ratio 80/313 (25.56%) compares published counts. Exact membership of the 313 could not be checked. Of the 16,942 published registered rows, 16,862 lack a figure row, including 361 registered FDR calls. The local testing family includes another 94 unmapped rows (17,036 tested in total).

The figure has 80/80 paired rows, 80/80 nonzero pairs and 78/80 same-sign pairs. These meet the v2 numerical direction thresholds for the selected panel. Cohort compatibility remains unresolved, and the figure provides no signed quantitative author estimates for a comparison spec.
mouse_hypo_hypoxia_gse162673.conclusion: Direction agrees for 78 of the 80 author-selected genes. Bcl11a and Egr4 have negative registered coefficients. All 2,123 reviewed pairs agree in direction. The median absolute log2 difference is 0.06780, the maximum is 2.92329 for Snord82, and the registered-to-author RMS effect ratio is 0.91853.

Printed FDR < 0.05 gives 1,323 calls in S1 and 16 in the registered table. The saved join gives 1,220 author, 15 registered and 14 shared calls. Including Oaz2 gives 1,221, 15 and 14. Eight author FDR values equal 0.05 at published precision. Stxbp5l has no paired author FDR. Zfp871 has author FDR 0.0657.

Including Oaz2 brings coverage to 2,123/2,301 (92.26%) and 2,123/13,709 (15.49%). Genes outside the worksheet have unassessed author effects and inference.

The v2 minimum is 30 pairs, 90% relevant coverage and compatible cohort, contrast, features and effects. coverage.note: Figure 7 covers genes selected through DIABLO sparse partial least squares discriminant analysis. The plot shows day-39 cross-tissue Pearson correlations with |r| > 0.80. Of 29 printed hypothalamic effects, 28 pair (96.55% of the selected reference, 0.204% of 13,700 published DE rows). Local provenance records 15,110 tested rows, including 1,410 unpublished unmapped rows. Figure 4B gives directions for 50 labels. All 41 unambiguous pairs agree (82% of labels). Seven lack a published coefficient and two labels resolve to the same registered key. The figures share 11 labels.

pig_hypo_low_growth_gse324226.criteria: Use every printed Figure 7 hypothalamic coefficient, the authors' low-relative-to-high orientation and one-to-one identifier matches. For a selected reference, author-concordance-v2 requires 30 paired effects, at least 90% coverage of selected author genes and compatible cohort, contrast, identifiers and effect definitions. Both correlations must reach 0.90, or same-gene direction agreement must reach 90% across at least 30 nonzero pairs covering at least 90% of all pairs. The separate Figure 4B sign check cannot add numerical pairs.
pig_hypo_low_growth_gse324226.conclusion: All 28 paired Figure 7 coefficients agree in direction (Pearson 0.9954, Spearman 0.9854). These represent 28 of 29 selected author genes and fall two pairs short of the concordance minimum. rat_hypo_fructose_gse56238.basis: Compare every assignable colored node with the sign of the registered fructose-minus-chow coefficient. Count a repeated gene once per figure. coverage.note: All 20 distinct colored genes in Figure 5b pair. In Figure 1, 15 of 17 distinct colored labels identify a single gene, and all 15 pair. C1q(a,b,c) and C4(a,b) each have a shared color. Paper-specific coverage is confined to these pathways. Whole-list discovery overlap and genome-wide paired author estimates remain unknown.

rat_hypo_fructose_gse56238.criteria: Use all distinct, individually identifiable colored nodes in each figure, with fructose versus chow fixed across genes. Preserve the printed stars in the original paper, including the Pomc star. The 2018 panel has no per-gene significance criterion. Assess each reference separately under author-concordance-v2. Each has fewer than the required 30 pairs, and neither gives exact paired coefficients for correlation.
rat_hypo_fructose_gse56238.conclusion: The selected figures support direct directional comparisons. The original paper has one unexplained sign reversal and nine marked discoveries that miss the registered threshold. The follow-up supports 15 individual directions. Neither reference establishes genome-wide concordance.

rat_hypo_hfd_wtts_gse100349.basis: The full_results scope covers inspection of the entire printed S2 worksheet. Its M:R values were compared with the registered gene-summed edgeR-QL output to diagnose attribution. A second calculation compares HFD minus chow group means on the displayed E:L scale.

The author’s Chapter 3 archive preserves the same worksheet values. S3 gives site counts, S4–S5 characterize selected sites, and Figure 5 used an independent 40-day qPCR cohort.

Section 2.3 describes RNA pooling and a control technical replicate, while §2.4 describes hypothalamic libraries from four individual male rats per diet. GEO describes eight adult male Long-Evans rats after 36 days. ENA and the registered sample sheet identify eight distinct BioSamples, four per arm. Workbook library IDs differ from GEO titles. Of 344 S3 sites with a unique matching GEO chromosome, strand and coordinate, 11 have all eight counts identical in the listed order. These records establish the diet groups, but leave animal selection, pooling and the fitted library key unresolved.

contrast.note: The biological contrast is 36-day HFD/DIO versus standard chow. The registered coefficient is groupcase, with chow as baseline. S2 labels E:H as control and I:L as HFD. Section 2.7 defines HFD increases as positive for differential polyadenylation sites. The original fitted gene coefficient’s orientation remains unconfirmed. The descriptive comparison uses HFD mean minus chow mean.

features.note: All 13,266 S2 gene IDs are unique. The specified one-to-one symbol rule, with deposited gene-ID agreement, retains 9,395 pairs and excludes 40 S2 rows carrying 20 repeated symbols. Checking all registered symbols with a single deposited gene ID recovers two additional unambiguous ID pairs, Mycbp2 (gene31580) and Anp32a (gene20591). Every S2 M:R tuple matches exactly one S1 site. Those site IDs span 1 through 13,266 and none has the S2 row’s printed symbol.

effects.note: For literal S2 log2 fold changes versus registered effects, Pearson r = −0.008020, Spearman rho = −0.004849, and 4,724 of 9,395 nonzero signs agree. These metrics have no confirmed gene-level interpretation. Subtracting control from HFD mean normalized expression (E:L) yields r = 0.857791, rho = 0.891378 and 8,291 matching signs. The transformation of those displayed values is insufficiently documented to treat that difference as a fitted log2 fold change.

inference.note: S2 has 13,170 finite raw P and 5,969 finite adjusted P values, each attributable to an S1 site. At raw P < 0.01 there are 135 printed S2 calls, 73 gene calls in the paper and 93 calls in the 9,439 published registered rows. No calls overlap on 9,324 jointly finite unique-symbol pairs. The two S2 labels at adjusted P < 0.10 are LOC108352883 (unannotated site 10545) and Reln (Rgs10 site 3502). No published registered row has FDR < 0.10 or < 0.05. The edgeR correction includes 11,937 tested features, of which 2,498 have no published gene row. The zero-call counts apply only to the published output. Gene-level author inference remains unassessed.

coverage.note: The original join covers 9,395 of 9,439 published registered genes (99.53%) and 9,395 of 13,266 printed S2 rows (70.82%). It excludes 25 registered symbols absent from S2 and 19 repeated in S2. The author-side exclusions are 3,831 unique unmatched rows and 40 duplicate-symbol rows. Requiring one deposited gene ID for each registered symbol and matching that ID and symbol to S2 gives 9,397 pairs. Of the remaining 42 registered genes, 26 have a deposited ID absent from S2 and 16 combine multiple deposited IDs. These are counts of identifiable rows. Coverage of genuine author gene coefficients remains unknown.

rat_hypo_hfd_wtts_gse100349.criteria: Use all rows and the two stated identifier rules without reference to effects or significance. Check all six S2 fitted fields, including missing-value positions, against all S1 sites. For displayed expression use HFD mean minus chow mean. Use the journal’s raw P < 0.01 and adjusted P < 0.10 and the project FDR < 0.05. For a full result table, author-concordance-v2 requires compatible cohort, contrast, identifiers and effect definitions, at least 30 pairs and at least 90% registered-output coverage. It also requires both correlations ≥ 0.90 or ≥ 90% matching directions among at least 30 nonzero pairs covering ≥ 90% of all pairs. Neither diagnostic supplies attributable fitted gene effects.
rat_hypo_hfd_wtts_gse100349.conclusion: The accessible S2 worksheet supports a descriptive comparison of the named genes’ normalized expression. Its printed model statistics cannot be attributed to those genes from public evidence. A corrected original fit and library key are required for a direct gene-result comparison specification or verification sign-off.

rat_hypo_ozone_gse133293.basis: We took log2 of each published linear SHAM ozone/air fold-change ratio in Table 1B and compared it with the corresponding registered limma groupcase coefficient. Every row in the hypothalamus panel entered the comparison.
rat_hypo_ozone_gse133293.reference: Henriquez et al., Toxicological Sciences (DOI 10.1093/toxsci/kfz182), Table 1B and supplementary methods. The EPA workbook (DOI 10.23719/1503697, worksheet “Table 1 No data”, embedded image28.emf) independently corroborates the publisher’s 40 symbols and rounded ratios, including Slco1c1 at 0.53. GSE133293 and ENA PRJNA551004 supply the matrix, sample metadata and run identities.

cohort.note: The original study sampled whole hypothalamus from male Wistar-Kyoto rats. The four air and four ozone SHAM samples (GSM3905188–GSM3905195) each have a distinct BioSample, registered expression column and matching ENA run. The reported tissue comparison excludes brainstem and AD arms.

contrast.note: Table 1B labels SH O3 / SH air. Ozone exposure was 0.8 ppm for four hours, with filtered air as the baseline. The registered groupcase coefficient has the same numerator and denominator.

features.note: The 40 Table 1B symbols match unique registered rows exactly, including case, with zero ambiguous or missing keys. GEO documents removal of genes with fewer than two counts across all samples. The deposited matrix contains 22,587 distinct gene labels. Applying the registered variance filter (>1×10⁻⁸ on the eight log-expression values) recovered exactly the 20,845 published identifiers. The original authors’ contrast-specific tested and adjusted-P universes remain unknown.

effects.note: Table 1B presents SHAM ozone/air ratios rounded to two decimal places. The paper specifies DESeq2 on rounded counts. It does not describe exactly how the published ratios were obtained from the fit. Log2 of each reported ratio and the registered ozone-minus-air mean log2(normalized count + 1) both describe the direction of change on a log2 scale. The maximum difference between the GEO-derived mean difference and the registered coefficient on this panel is 1.02×10⁻¹⁴. Against the published effects, the median absolute log2 difference is 0.24700, the maximum is 1.86760 (Hif3a), and the registered-to-author RMS ratio is 1.39909.

inference.note: The authors used DESeq2 1.10.1 and report 311 increases and 257 decreases in SHAM hypothalamus at FDR ≤ 0.10. Table 1B establishes that all 40 selected genes met that threshold. Registered limma calls 170 genes at the same cutoff, including 38 of the 40. Local adjusted P is 0.30869 for Amer2 and 0.10390 for Zbtb16. Author call status for the 132 local discoveries outside this panel cannot be inferred from their omission. At local FDR < 0.05, 26 panel genes and 40 other genes pass. All 66 lack numeric author adjusted P values in the reviewed material. The full positive-list intersection and the authors’ calls at 0.05 remain unknown.

coverage.note: The comparison covers 40/40 published panel entries, 40/568 reported author discoveries (7.04%) and 40/20,845 registered effects (0.192%). Table 1B gives no effect for the other 528 author discoveries or the other 20,805 registered genes.

rat_hypo_ozone_gse133293.criteria: Use every Table 1B gene. The selected reference is the coverage denominator. Author-concordance-v2 requires compatible cohort, contrast, identifiers and effect definitions, ≥30 paired genes and ≥90% coverage, plus either Pearson and Spearman both ≥0.90, or ≥90% same-gene sign agreement among ≥30 nonzero pairs covering ≥90% of pairs. Magnitude and inference are contextual.
rat_hypo_ozone_gse133293.conclusion: 40 of 40 nonzero pairs agree in direction. Pearson is 0.97595 and Spearman is 0.88509. The directional route of author-concordance-v2 passes for the selected genes. The correlation route falls below its Spearman cutoff. The table provides selected-gene effect evidence only. Whole-universe inference and full verification remain open.

rat_mbh_edc_gse168151.basis: Compare the sign and magnitude of each registered edgeR-QL log2 fold change with log2(EDC qPCR mean / control qPCR mean) for every F1 P21 MBH-PoA mRNA measurement in Figures 6A and S10A. Use the numerical means printed in Tables S3 and S5.
rat_mbh_edc_gse168151.reference: López-Rodríguez et al., EHP8795, supplemental PDF ehp8795.s001.acco.pdf, Table S3 on PDF page 18 and Table S5 on PDF page 22. Figure 6A and Figure S10A identify the generation, age and mRNA assay. The preprint describes the same experiment.

cohort.note: Species, sex, age and anatomical dissection align. The qPCR panels use six animals per arm, with six litters per arm specified for Figure 6A. GEO treatment fields and the sample sheet document four F1 libraries per arm. Animal overlap and the RNA library-to-litter mapping are unknown.

contrast.note: Maternal-lineage EDC mixture relative to vehicle in the P21 F1 female MBH-PoA. Both effect signs use EDC minus control on a log2 scale. F3, other ages, cross-fostering, protein, methylation and chromatin measurements fall outside this comparison.

features.note: All six qPCR targets join uniquely to the registered table. Five use exact rat gene symbols. NCBI Gene 360616 records Darpp32 as an alias for Ppp1r1b. The RNA-seq testing universe used by the authors is unknown.

effects.note: The qPCR log2 ratios use rounded group means after efficiency-adjusted β-actin normalization and scaling to the control mean. The registered edgeR-QL coefficients use TMM-normalized libraries. Actb itself has registered log2FC +0.734170 (BH 0.00002146), so equal reference scaling across assays cannot be assumed. Four of six nonzero signs agree. Pearson is 0.599705, Spearman is 0.485714 and the median absolute log2 difference is 1.135646. The qPCR and RNA-seq values are +1.770 and −0.192 for Drd1, and +0.084 and −1.098 for Crh.

inference.note: Figure 6A specifies two-way ANOVA with Sidak comparisons. Table S5 labels the S10A values as P values. At 0.05, three targets meet the reported qPCR threshold and five meet the registered RNA-seq BH threshold. Drd1 has qPCR P = 0.016 and RNA-seq BH = 0.636. Crh has qPCR P = 0.82 and RNA-seq BH = 0.0124. Only Th and Dnm1 meet both assay thresholds. The original F1 RNA-seq P values and FDR are unavailable for comparison.

coverage.note: All six author-selected qPCR targets in Figures 6A and S10A were paired, covering 100% of that reference and 0.046472% of the 12,911 published registered genes. The registered BH family includes 14,587 tested rows, of which 1,676 had no mapped symbol and were withheld. Figure S9 reports F1 GO enrichment. The reviewed sources supplied no full F1 gene-level author RNA-seq table.

rat_mbh_edc_gse168151.criteria: Include every P21 F1 mRNA target in Figures 6A and S10A, in the published treatment direction, regardless of significance. Author-concordance-v2 requires at least 30 pairs, at least 90% coverage of the relevant reference or output, and compatible cohort, contrast, identifiers and effect definitions. Either both correlations must reach 0.90, or at least 90% of nonzero pairs must agree in direction, with at least 30 nonzero pairs covering at least 90% of all pairs. Magnitude differences and assay-specific P values are descriptive.
rat_mbh_edc_gse168151.conclusion: The selected qPCR and registered RNA-seq point estimates agree in direction for Th, Dnm1, Ppp1r1b and Nr3c1. Drd1 and Crh have opposite signs. The six pairs fall below the v2 minimum, and both numerical routes also fall below their agreement thresholds. The study’s original gene-level RNA-seq analysis remains unassessed.

rat_mbh_perinatal_des_gse225359.basis: Registered R 4.6.0 edgeR quasi-likelihood output for track mbh against the P90 DES12 coefficient and adjusted P in the Figures 3–7 workbook. All deposited reference rows were considered.

AL and AM give the P90 MBH DES12 log2 fold change versus vehicle and adjusted P. The DEG workbook, Figure 3D and Table 2 cross-check the column assignment within the same experiment.

Of 22,616 finite author effects, 6,022 lack a published symbol mapping, 3,580 have uniquely mapped symbols outside the DE table and 12 belong to multi-ID symbols. Six published coefficients combine source IDs and remain unpaired.

effects.note: Both coefficients express treatment versus vehicle on the log2 scale. DESeq2 and edgeR-QL use different estimators. Pearson 0.9021, Spearman 0.9888, and 98.25% directional agreement. The median absolute log2FC difference is 0.01624 and the registered-to-author RMS effect ratio is 1.654. The magnitude difference remains material to interpretation.

inference.note: Section 2.6 specifies pairwise DESeq2, adjusted P < 0.05 and no fold-change cutoff. Section 2.9 prints adjusted P > 0.05. The dose labels in the deposited DEG sheet resolve the conflict for this contrast. Exactly 2,498 D12-labelled IDs meet the lower-tail rule, while 13,270 other finite adjusted P values exceed 0.05. The registered edgeR-QL fit adjusts across 14,615 tested rows, including 1,607 unpublished rows. It reports 847 discoveries among 13,008 published coefficients. Of the 13,002 pairs with finite adjusted P on both sides, 828 pass in both analyses, 1,453 only in the author analysis and 19 only in the registered analysis. Another 217 author discoveries have no unique published effect pair. Every registered discovery has a finite author test. The workbook omits raw P values. Missing author adjusted P values remain unassessed.

coverage.note: 13,002/13,008 (99.95%) of registered effects and 13,002/22,616 (57.49%) of finite author effects pair. The full-results policy uses the registered denominator. All 13,002 pairs have two nonzero effects and finite adjusted P values. The source includes another 10,267 rows without a finite target effect.

rat_mbh_perinatal_des_gse225359.criteria: Use every finite, uniquely paired effect with its published sign. For full results author-concordance-v2 requires at least 30 pairs covering at least 90% of the registered output, with Pearson and Spearman each at least 0.90 or at least 90% same direction among 30 or more nonzero pairs covering at least 90% of all pairs. Cohort, contrast, identifiers and effect definitions must also be compatible. Magnitudes and FDR calls provide context.
rat_mbh_perinatal_des_gse225359.conclusion: Both numerical routes pass for the published effects of the registered P90 MBH contrast. The registered effects have a larger RMS magnitude, and the two analyses identify different discovery sets. The contributions of specific model settings and the maternal litter membership of the ten libraries remain unresolved.

rat_pvn_sodium_depletion_gse145431.basis: Compare the RNA-seq directions explicitly attributed to this study’s PVN transcriptome in the Results and Discussion with the sign of the registered Furo10-minus-control log2 fold change. Retain the complete nine-gene follow-up panel as a distinct denominator and add Creb3l1, which the Discussion names separately. The paper describes read counts above 30 and biological considerations for selecting the follow-up panel. The comparison applies no further count or significance cutoff.
rat_pvn_sodium_depletion_gse145431.reference: Dutra et al., Neuroendocrinology 111, 70–86, DOI 10.1159/000505997. See Experiment 3 and the RNA-seq methods (p. 72), the named panel and Figure 5 caption (p. 78), Figure 5 (p. 79), and the Discussion’s Creb3l1 statement (p. 83). features.note: Each of the ten text-named genes resolves to a single deposited Ensembl feature. The Results spelling Miss18a resolves to Mis18a through the protein name, the qPCR text and rat GeneID 288272. ENSRNOG00000021555 meets the registered expression cutoff in only one of the three libraries required and has no DE row. Creb3l1 maps to ENSRNOG00000005413. The other nine genes, including Creb3l1, have unique registered coefficients.

Adding Creb3l1 gives six increases and three decreases, all concordant. Figure 5 shows row-standardized per-library pseudocounts. The named directions support a sign comparison only.

Seven of the eight paired follow-up genes, plus Creb3l1, meet registered raw P < 0.05. Ephx2 agrees in sign at registered P = 0.10413. None of the nine paired genes meets registered BH FDR < 0.05. The registered BH family includes all 16,340 tested rows.

coverage.note: The follow-up panel contributes eight of nine directions (88.89%). Adding the Discussion result gives nine of ten text-named directions (90.0%) and nine of 13,619 published registered rows (0.0661%). The 100 labeled heatmap rows have no verified crosswalk to the 94 reported genes. The six GEO count columns supply expression inputs only. Overlap with the complete author discovery list and tested universe remains unknown.

rat_pvn_sodium_depletion_gse145431.criteria: Retain every explicit text direction for Experiment 3, including genes with absent coefficients or registered P ≥ 0.05. Use the paper’s biological orientation and compare nonzero signs. The nine-gene panel has 88.89% reference coverage. The expanded text selection reaches 90% reference coverage, but its nine pairs fall below the author-concordance-v2 minimum of 30. The paper supplies insufficient data for coefficient correlations, magnitude agreement or a numerical comparison spec.
rat_pvn_sodium_depletion_gse145431.conclusion: The nine available signs agree within the ten text-named PVN genes. Pool composition, gene-level author inference and the mapping from Figure 5 to the discovery list remain unresolved. No registered contrast earns full verification.

rat_pvn_stress_gse261833.basis: The five labels in Figure 4A define the comparison set. Read their direction and screen membership from the model-versus-control plot and compare with the same symbols in the registered pvn DE table. The restored track’s rounded rows give the same signs and cutoff counts.

The five model libraries (GSM8152695–GSM8152699) and five untreated libraries (GSM8152685–GSM8152689) match the registered sheet by accession, sample label and treatment. features.note: Each Figure 4A label matches one registered symbol, using Hif3a as printed on the plot for the caption’s Hif3α. Four labels each occur on one deposited feature. GEO calls both ENSRNOG00000013167 and ENSRNOG00000033321 Hmgb2. They map to registered Hmgb2 (+0.694923) and Hmgb2l1 (−0.048282), respectively. The plotted Hmgb2 feature or aggregation is unknown.

effects.note: All five markers lie on the positive side of Figure 4A and all five same-symbol registered coefficients are positive. The four labels with a unique deposited feature also agree in sign. Author edgeR log2 fold changes and registered differences in mean log2(FPKM + 1) estimate the stress effect differently. The plot supplies no exact author coefficients for magnitude or correlation checks.

inference.note: Methods define the edgeR 3.42.4 screen as raw P < 0.05 and absolute log2FC ≥ 0.5. Results use > 0.5. Both boundaries give the same registered calls. All five same-symbol rows have raw P < 0.05, four meet the combined rule and none have BH FDR < 0.05. Clec7a is a known screen disagreement. Exact author P and FDR values are unavailable. The cause of the aggregate count difference remains unresolved.

coverage.note: Figure 4A names 5 of the 503 reported DEGs. All 5 labels match registered symbols, representing 5 of the 16,117 published genes. The registered fit also tested 6,238 unpublished unmapped rows, for a total of 22,355. The authors’ tested universe and full screen membership are unavailable.

rat_pvn_stress_gse261833.criteria: Include every Figure 4A label, orient model minus untreated control and use each published fold-change boundary with raw P < 0.05. Both author-concordance-v2 routes require at least 30 paired genes, at least 90% relevant reference/output coverage and compatible definitions. Five named directions fall below the minimum.
rat_pvn_stress_gse261833.conclusion: The selected comparison establishes five matching symbol-level directions. Clec7a’s screen membership differs, and Hmgb2’s feature-level direction is unresolved. The aggregate totals remain unreconciled. This comparison supports neither a numerical magnitude assessment nor author-concordance-v2 or full contrast sign-off.

rat_rph_noise_stress_gse229159.basis: Current registered rPH edgeR-QL coefficient for seven daily loud-noise exposures relative to no stress.
rat_rph_noise_stress_gse229159.reference: Campeau et al., Supplementary Table S1, pages 2–11, complete Control vs. 7 Loud noise exposures block. The authors selected genes at BH-adjusted P ≤ 0.05.

cohort.note: Independent adult male rat rPH specimens were collected 24 hours after the last exposure. GEO has six rats per arm. The manuscript excluded one library per arm before DE. A reconstruction using counts and all 405 published baseMeans identifies GSM7156104 (PH01, RS7) and GSM7156123 (PH20, control) as the two extra animals in the registered contrast. The authors' DESeq2 baseMeans reflect 20 animals across four arms.

contrast.note: Both effects compare rPH at the same endpoint after seven daily exposures with no-stress controls. Figure 2 defines direction relative to control. The one- and three-exposure pairwise contrasts and the separate in situ cohort are outside scope.

features.note: Used the printed rat Ensembl ID and the registered feature map. All 405 IDs are distinct. Exactly 358 map one-to-one to a published effect, including eight with different printed and current symbol labels. The 47 unmapped IDs remain unpaired. Five of their printed labels occur in the registered table under other stable IDs.

effects.note: Both studies estimate a log2 fold change in the same direction. For the 358 paired effects, Pearson is 0.991593, Spearman is 0.986957, and 358 of 358 nonzero pairs have the same sign. Median absolute difference is 0.026445 log2 units. The paired RMS registered-to-author effect ratio is 0.963731.

inference.note: The authors used DESeq2 1.28.1 Wald tests and BH-adjusted P ≤ 0.05. All 405 S1 adjusted P values in this contrast are below 0.05. The registered two-arm edgeR quasi-likelihood fit used TMM normalization and BH adjustment across 15,754 tested rows. The published output contains 12,993 symbol-level effects and 55 discoveries at FDR < 0.05. Of 358 paired genes, 49 pass both cutoffs and 309 pass only the author cutoff. The other six published discoveries lack a paired author adjusted P. Bounds from the published raw and adjusted P values establish 61 discoveries across the full fit, including six unpublished rows. The identities of those six rows are unknown from the published table. S1 omits raw P values.

coverage.note: The comparison retains all 405 selected author IDs. It covers 358/405 (88.40%) of the published selection and 358/12,993 (2.76%) of published registered effects. The unfiltered author testing universe was not located.

rat_rph_noise_stress_gse229159.criteria: Apply author-concordance-v2 to all paired, uniquely mapped effects. For this selected list the coverage denominator is all 405 reference rows. Require at least 30 pairs, 90% selected-reference coverage and supported cohort, contrast, identifier and effect compatibility. The numerical alternatives are Pearson and Spearman each ≥0.90, or ≥90% direction agreement on at least 30 nonzero pairs covering ≥90% of all pairs. Report adjusted-P calls and magnitudes as context.
rat_rph_noise_stress_gse229159.conclusion: Both numerical alternatives pass on the 358 pairs. The registered fit includes one additional rat per comparison arm. Forty-seven author IDs lack a published registered effect, leaving the identifier assessment limited and selected-reference coverage at 88.40%, below the 90% requirement. The evidence supports a selected-gene comparison without v2 acceptance or full verification.

human_htnsc_differentiation_gse214877.basis: Registered TMM edgeR-QL groupcase logFC on the hypothalamic_nsc track, read in htNSC-minus-hPSC orientation.
human_htnsc_differentiation_gse214877.reference: Sulistio et al., bioRxiv 10.1101/2024.05.23.595504, Figure 1D in both versions. All 37 labeled rows of the bulk expression heatmap, restricted to its three PSC and three htNSC columns.

cohort.note: The study names GSE214877 and the plotted group sizes and cell types correspond to the registered arms. Figure 1D gives no per-column GSMs. Two control titles/count columns conflict with GEO and ENA cell-line fields. H9-derived htNSCs have distinct batches and DIVs. Donor independence and line-adjusted effects are unresolved.

contrast.note: Figure 1D labels PSC and htNSC columns. The registered contrast supplies the orientation used to compare them, with higher expression in htNSCs corresponding to positive logFC. The four adult GTEx regions are outside this comparison.

features.note: All 37 displayed gene symbols occur in the deposited counts. Exact, unique joins recover 33 of them in the registered output. AGRP, TBR1, NEUROD6 and PITX3 have no registered row.

effects.note: The color key runs from +1.5 (yellow) to −1.5 (purple). Reading across each gene’s row, we found complete separation between the two culture groups for 21 joined genes in both renderings. The figure and bulk methods leave the exact transformation unspecified. Only ordinal directions were compared. Numerical author coefficients, magnitude agreement and correlations remain unassessed.

inference.note: The bulk supplement names DESeq2. Figure 1D supplies no gene-level P, adjusted P or significant calls for the culture contrast, so inference and significant-set overlap remain unassessed.

coverage.note: The denominator includes all 37 selected markers. At most 33/37 (89.19%) have a registered row. Of these, 21 yield a plotted direction and 12 are indeterminate. The usable direction pairs cover 21/37 (56.76%) of the selected panel. No full author tested-gene table was located.

human_htnsc_differentiation_gse214877.criteria: Read all 37 figure rows before joining registered effects. Use the registered htNSC-minus-hPSC orientation. Call a sign only when the intervals pooled across the two PDF renderings put every htNSC tile on the same side of every PSC tile. Keep ambiguous and unmatched rows in the panel denominator. Author-concordance-v2 requires at least 30 paired genes, 90% relevant coverage and compatible definitions. Its numerical routes require either Pearson and Spearman correlations of at least 0.90 or at least 90% sign agreement among at least 30 nonzero pairs covering at least 90% of all pairs. The figure supports ordinal comparisons only.
human_htnsc_differentiation_gse214877.conclusion: All 21 readable paired directions agree. Both the 30-pair minimum and 90% selected-reference coverage requirement are unmet. The cell-line conflict limits cohort interpretation. No numerical comparison spec or full verification is supported.

mouse_hypo_hfd_tc_gse305719.basis: The registered edgeR-QL groupcase coefficient comes directly from the DE table. For Figure 13A, the author-side comparison requires two reconstructions. The 72 intermediate libraries identify the unlabeled rows, then the colors of the six week-12 and six day-0 libraries bound the difference between the group means. Both analyses use the same mice.
mouse_hypo_hfd_tc_gse305719.reference: Oku et al., DOI 10.1587/nolta.17.186, Figure 13A (printed p. 204), Table I and Table II. Biological replicate order and gene identifiers come from GSE305719 and the paper-linked plotting and clustering code. Reproducible inputs, SHA-256 values, every figure row and its interval are in data/author-validation/continued-sources/GSE305719/codex-2026-11-21.

cohort.note: GEO identifies the tissue as hypothalamus. The registry calls the bulk track whole hypothalamus. The paper describes terminal dissections of separate male mice at each time point and lists no hypothalamus exclusions. All six day-0 libraries (GSM9182784–GSM9182789) and all six week-12 libraries (GSM9182862–GSM9182867) match the registered sheet.

contrast.note: Mean at HFD week 12 minus mean at day 0, when high-fat feeding began after chow acclimatization. Positive means higher at week 12. Age and duration of feeding vary together. The study lacks an age-matched chow arm.

features.note: Both disjoint intermediate-library partitions recovered all 179 distinct symbols. The order agrees with the authors' alphabetical cluster order and includes all ten hypothalamic Table II genes. The registered feature map maps every symbol to itself. Exactly 170 occur in the registered DE table.

effects.note: Figure 13A standardizes log2 trimmed-TPM expression within each gene across the 84 hypothalamus libraries. Its endpoint mean difference is in gene-specific sample SD units. The registered effect is a TMM-normalized edgeR log2 fold change. Only signs were compared. At the primary color allowance, 147 pairs agree, nine have opposite signs and 14 additional paired intervals include zero. The intervals describe color resolution. They do not estimate sampling error.

inference.note: The reviewed paper, count deposit and code supply no gene-level author P value or FDR for week 12 versus day 0. The intervention scores rank genes, and the enrichment statistics concern gene sets. None of the 617 registered BH discoveries could be checked against an author endpoint statistic.

coverage.note: All 179 genes in the published Figure 13A cluster were retained. The 170 exact pairs cover 94.97% of the panel and 1.18% of the 14,376 registered genes. At the primary allowance, 156 directions are readable (91.76% of pairs and 87.15% of the panel). Nine panel genes lack a registered result and 14,206 registered genes are outside the panel.

mouse_hypo_hfd_tc_gse305719.criteria: Use the published cluster as selected. Identify rows without the endpoints, join by exact symbol and apply no significance or effect-size filter. Subtract day-0 from week-12 means. A positive lower bound or negative upper bound establishes sign under the published color bins with a one-RGB-level allowance. Keep zero-touching intervals indeterminate and report all denominators.
mouse_hypo_hfd_tc_gse305719.conclusion: At the stated one-level RGB allowance, 147/156 determinate directions agree (94.23%). The selected-panel fractions reach the v2 numerical cutoffs descriptively. In a sensitivity check allowing two RGB levels per channel, only 147/170 pairs have determinate signs (86.47%), below the 90% directional coverage cutoff. The reconstruction and different effect units support a descriptive sign comparison only. Author concordance and full contrast sign-off remain unassessed.
